newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Dewan Salman down 3.06 pct.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Dewan Salman down 3.06 pct.

text.p: Pakistan's Dewan Salman Fibre slipped 1.35 rupees, or 3.06 percent, to 42.65 on Tuesday on expectations that local manufacturers would cut prices, dealers said.
Turnover of more than 1.1 million shares of Dewan Salman Fibres was recorded in early trade.

"Local manufacturers are likely to reduce fibre prices to make their products competitive with imports," dealer Ather Raouf said. "Although Dewan Salman's 1996/97 profits will be good, next year will be tough."
"It is not just Dewan Salman, the whole synthetic sector is faced with problems because of excess supply," he added.
Dewan Salman ends its financial year on June 30.
Dealer Mohammad Iqbal, however, said a cut in fibre prices would boost the sector in the long term, even if it temporarily depressed synthetic stocks prices, including Dewan Salman's.

"Local manufacturers demand a ban on fibre imports, which is resisted by the textile sector on the grounds that imported fibre costs less," he said. "If manufacturers cut fibre prices to stop imports, it would benefit the synthetic sector in the long run."
